subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

The best of both worlds

options.text: Stay strong in a difficult situation

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 4.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"The best of both worlds"** means to enjoy the advantages of two different things at the same time. (दोनों दुनिया की सबसे अच्छी चीजें) • **Example:** By working part-time and looking after her kids two days a week she managed to get the best of both worlds. • **"Good in every way"** refers to something that is beneficial and positive in all aspects. (हर तरह से अच्छा) • **Example:** This new policy is good in every way; it benefits the employees and the company alike. Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate meaning of** "The best of both worlds" is "Good in every way".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Everyone gets a chance** (हर किसी को मौका मिलता है): This phrase means that each person has the opportunity to participate. • **Example:** The new competition format ensures that everyone gets a chance to showcase their talents. • **Stay strong in a difficult situation** (कठिन परिस्थिति में मजबूत रहना): This phrase means to remain resilient and steadfast during tough times. • **Example:** She managed to stay strong in a difficult situation when her business faced financial troubles. • **Do a perfectly good job** (एक बहुत अच्छा काम करना): This phrase means to perform a task exceptionally well. • **Example:** He did a perfectly good job of organizing the event, and everyone praised his efforts. 48:Tcd9, The correct answer is: **Option 2.**
